How Minecraft Whitelist Management Works in Agrelha
System
Light
Dark
Clean
Export
A
Answer
Ask

Agrelha manages access through a non-destructive RCON probe, dual-write GitOps persistence, and environment-based UUID pre-resolution.

Probing uses a temporary /whitelist on probe to infer status because modern Minecraft dropped /whitelist status.1
Add and remove actions apply instantly via RCON and save to GitOps for restart persistence.1
The container resolves player names to UUIDs at boot using the WHITELIST environment variable.2
Every access change emits an immutable audit record with actor identity and target player.1

Applies to
Minecraft 1.13+
RCON protocol
GitOps dual-write

1
How does Agrelha probe whitelist status without modifying state?
Ask
Non-destructive whitelist probe
▶ Play messages
Open interactive view
/whitelist on
Whitelist is already turned on
/whitelist on (if was off)
Whitelist is now turned on
/whitelist off (immediate rollback)
Agrelha Engine
Minecraft Server
Legend
main request
return
security
message

Modern Minecraft removed /whitelist status. Agrelha issues /whitelist on and checks the response text. If the server answers with already, the whitelist was already active. If it answers with now, Agrelha immediately sends /whitelist off to restore disabled state.

▶ Step through
Probe Command ↗

Agrelha transmits /whitelist on across RCON.

Branch Check ↗

The parser inspects the response for already or now.

State Revert ↗

If now appeared, Agrelha sends /whitelist off instantly.

2
How are player access modifications kept in sync?
Ask
Dual-write GitOps & live RCON update
▶ Play messages
Open interactive view
Add player request
Patch whitelist.txt commit
/whitelist add player
/whitelist reload
Reloaded whitelist
Operator UI
Agrelha Core
GitOps Store
Minecraft Server
Legend
main request
return
security
message

Live server state and declarative GitOps configurations stay aligned through dual writes. A single API call modifies the in-memory game state and commits to whitelist.txt.

▶ Step through
GitOps Patch ↗

Agrelha writes the username into whitelist.txt in Git.

Live RCON Add ↗

Agrelha issues /whitelist add to admit the player immediately.

Live Reload ↗

Agrelha reloads server memory so changes take effect without restart.

3
Why does container startup require WHITELIST rather than WHITELIST_FILE?
Ask

The container entrypoint mc-image-helper handles usernames differently based on configuration format. Passing usernames via environment variable triggers PlayerDB and Mojang UUID lookups before server launch.

Approach	Startup UUID Resolution	Offline / Modded Safety	GitOps Compatibility
WHITELIST env var	
Online UUID
Automatic lookup
	
Pre-cached
High resilience
	
ConfigMap key mapping

WHITELIST_FILE mount	
Raw names
Skips image helper
	
Unresolved
Risk of join errors
	
Direct file volume
UUID resolution requirement

Passing declarative values through WHITELIST lets mc-image-helper query Mojang APIs before server startup. Mounting files directly leaves raw strings without UUID mappings in whitelist.json.

4
Access management checklist
Ask
Confirm RCON port 25575 responds with authenticated session
Verify WhitelistEnforced() returns accurate boolean without leaving whitelist enabled
Inspect Git repository history for automated mc-access commits
Ensure deployment passes WHITELIST environment variable from ConfigMap

AccessManager implementation

GEMINI.md:20–27
